# Places are made of slightly dead Spaces

Replying to: [[3q36phkpev9w72hff84srnw98d]]

In Yi Fu Tuan's conceptions, to make a Place, something of Place must die. A clearing acquires a name, paths, boundaries, and memories. A thousand possible ways through it collapse into a few familiar ones. Space, in Yi-Fu Tuan's sense, surrenders some freedom to become place.

But place makes new freedoms possible. A lab fixes the area of science you can reach, yet allows scientists to explore ideas that were previously unreachable.

And no scientist starts blank. They carry their previous labs and trainings, their places, into new spaces through their protocols, instruments, jargon, and even superstitions.

Perhaps space and place are not then opposites but phases of a continuous metamorphosis. We sacrifice possibility to create a foothold, then use that foothold to discover possibilities that could not previously exist.
